obtained.how: agency copy: Wisconsin DNR's own species sheet PDF

bibliography.checked_against: the sheet itself (p. 2 imprint; author line on pp. 3–5)
bibliography.corrections: the sheet names its authors and number: Dehring, T. & Krueger, C. C. 2008. Bullheads. Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, Bureau of Fisheries Management, PUBL-FM-706 08, July 2008 (covers black, brown and yellow bullhead)
bibliography.note: it uses the old names Ictalurus melas, I. nebulosus, I. natalis

claims.claim: brown bullheads bury themselves in leafy ooze and stop feeding (Wisconsin DNR 2008)
claims.source_value: said of bullheads in general (black, brown and yellow): as winter comes they 'stop feeding, become sluggish and often bury themselves in soft, leafy ooze along the shore'
claims.quote: stop feeding, become sluggish and often bury themselves in soft, leafy ooze along the shore
claims.conditions: popular species sheet; no data, place or temperature given; 'often', not always; the sheet links it to surviving winterkill
claims.note: write 'bullheads (the sheet covers all three species) often bury themselves…'; it is a general natural-history statement, not a brown-bullhead observation

claims.claim: brown bullheads loaf in weed beds by day and prowl after dark (Wisconsin DNR 2008)
claims.source_value: said of bullheads in general: 'Generally, bullheads remain inactive during the daylight hours, loafing in weed beds until night falls', then 'go out on the prowl' after dark
claims.quote: bullheads remain inactive during the daylight hours, loafing in weed beds until night falls
claims.conditions: popular species sheet covering black, brown and yellow bullhead; no data
claims.note: the content is there but for the genus, with 'Generally'; attribute it to bullheads, not brown bullhead specifically

notes: A five-page popular sheet; useful as a general description only. Other statements in it (not used by the paper): spawning April–July at 70–77 °F (21–25 °C); brown bullheads nest on rocky and sandy bottoms; 1,600–14,000 eggs; hatch in 5–10 days; parents guard about two weeks; maturity in 3–4 years; a length-at-age table (1 yr 2.8 in, 2 yr 7.7 in, 5 yr 9.3 in, 10 yr 13.5 in) not attributed to a species.
